source_semantics.scanner_metadata: The canonical generated ledger classifies this service row as mutation=false and risk=low; this evidence preserves that scanner metadata exactly rather than rewriting the generated contract.
source_semantics.claim_transition: The authoritative source method nevertheless performs a durable scheduler state transition inside a transaction: enabled due Synchronization/SEO Audit jobs whose last status is not Running are selected in due-time order and each claimed job receives LastStatus=Running plus LastRunUtc/UpdatedAtUtc set to the supplied UTC claim instant.
source_semantics.reclaim_boundary: Already-running, future, disabled and unsupported jobs are not claimed, and a completed claim cannot be selected again while its status remains Running.
source_semantics.dispatch_boundary: ClaimDueJobs claims work only. It does not create an execution record, advance NextRunUtc, or perform the eventual job payload; those responsibilities remain separate from this service member.

laravel_adaptation.persistence: Uses the existing tenant-owned scheduled_tasks table rather than introducing duplicate scheduler persistence.
laravel_adaptation.tenant_scope: Every candidate read, conditional claim update and returned-row lookup is constrained to the active TenantContext tenant_id.
laravel_adaptation.atomicity: Candidate selection and claims execute in one database transaction with row locking where supported plus a second tenant/due/status/type guarded conditional update before a row is accepted as claimed.
laravel_adaptation.supported_work: Only the Laravel scheduler equivalents sync and seo_audit are claimable; backup/report schedule types remain outside this canonical member.
laravel_adaptation.state_transition: Claimed rows receive last_status=Running and last_run_at/updated_at equal to the supplied UTC instant; next_run_at is intentionally not advanced.
laravel_adaptation.dispatch_boundary: No operation_executions row is created by this adapter, preserving the canonical claim-only service boundary and keeping existing dispatchDueSchedules behavior separate.

proofs: active tenant claims only enabled due sync and seo_audit work in deterministic due-time order
future, disabled, already-running and unsupported scheduled work remains untouched
foreign-tenant due work is explicitly absent from claimed results and remains untouched in persistence
claimed rows transition to Running at the supplied UTC claim instant without advancing next_run_at
claim operation creates no operation_executions record
a second claim cannot reclaim an already-running row
acceptance.external_runtime: No live WordPress/provider/email/payment/DNS/production evidence is required because this operation is a local scheduler persistence transition.
